_README: Frozen native-fixture verification contract (spec section 7 in shared/ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md; Issue #20, Epic 3). The parity harness (test_vectors.json) CANNOT catch a wrong adapter flip because its vectors are defined as the adapter's OUTPUT, downstream of the y-flip + horizontal mirror. The only way to verify the flips is to run the real native pose estimator on a known pose and assert the adapter's output satisfies the geometric invariants below. This file freezes WHAT every adapter must satisfy, so both platforms assert the same thing -- the same discipline that froze the alphabet against one canonical chart. Human-readable companion: shared/native_fixtures/NATIVE-FIXTURES.md.
_frame: All coordinates and invariants are in the POST-ADAPTER frame, identical to keypoint_contract.json and spec section 4.2: normalized [0,1], +x = SIGNER'S RIGHT, y-up, signer's perspective. Note this is NOT the camera/image frame the pose images are drawn in -- the image is the observer's view (signer facing the camera), and the adapter's mirror + y-flip relate the two. That relationship is exactly what these invariants pin.

_invariant_dsl.operand: a keypoint component, '<name>.<x|y>', e.g. 'right_wrist.x'. Names are keypoint_contract.json.keypoints.names.
_invariant_dsl.pins: which adapter transform a violation implicates (y-flip / horizontal mirror).
_invariant_dsl.evaluation: Invariants are RELATIONAL on purpose: they hold for ANY correct adapter output regardless of exact coordinates, so the real estimator's coords (which differ run-to-run and across Vision vs ML Kit) still satisfy them. reference_post_adapter below is a SYNTHETIC ideal output used only to self-test the invariants and the decoder; it is not the expected estimator output.

poses.name: right_arm_out
poses.description: Signer's right arm straight out to the signer's right (position id 2, 0deg); left arm straight down (position id 0, -90deg). Asymmetric ON PURPOSE: an asymmetric pose distinguishes a wrong horizontal mirror from a left/right anatomical-label swap, which a symmetric pose cannot (ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md section 3b).

invariants.why: id 2 (0deg) points along +x = signer's right, so the extended wrist is at greater x than its shoulder. A missed or extra mirror puts it at lesser x.
id 2 is horizontal, so the out-arm's wrist and shoulder sit at nearly equal height. A wrong y-flip tilts it off horizontal.
id 0 (-90deg) points down; in a y-up frame the wrist is below the shoulder. A wrong y-flip inverts this.
Signer faces the camera and +x = signer's right, so the right shoulder is at greater x than the left. The cleanest single mirror/label check (ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md sections 1, 3b).

poses.name: arms_down
poses.description: Both arms straight down (position id 0 / id 0). The symmetric sanity pose: pins the y-flip independently on each arm and the mirror via shoulder order.

invariants.why: Left arm down (id 0) ⇒ wrist below shoulder in a y-up frame.
Right arm down (id 0) ⇒ wrist below shoulder in a y-up frame.
Right shoulder at greater x than the left in the signer's perspective.
